text: Someone went through your things in the night. Your coin purse is lighter.
{npc}'s stores were ransacked overnight. Nobody saw anything. Nobody ever sees anything.
A fire took {npc}'s home in the small hours. The bucket line was slow to form — what's the point, it'll be back tomorrow. The smoke stain on the sky won't be.
{npc} is gone. The door stands open, breakfast half-made. Drag marks toward the outskirts.
{npc} didn't wake up where they should have. Some say they walked out the gate before dawn and just kept walking.
A mob formed in the square last night over nothing — a look, a rumor, a loaf. It dissolved at dawn, but everyone remembers who held a torch.
Chanting from the old mill past midnight. Hooded figures. They call themselves the Children of the Turning Day, and their number grows.
{npc} stood in the square at midnight screaming at the sky to just get it over with. People closed their shutters and listened.
Candles in every window last night — somebody organized a vigil. For a few hours the town remembered it was a town.
Nothing happened last night. No voices, no footsteps, no dogs. The town has begun holding its breath, and the silence is worse than the screaming.
